 After escaping Providence over the weekend, the Huskers return home to begin the week looking to defend their new spot in the AP Top 25. Geoff Exstrom | Share on Facebook Share on X Add us as a preferred source The Nebraska men's basketball team returns home Tuesday night to defend its home floor against Lindenwood. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect In this story:
 Nebraska Cornhuskers It may have taken AP voters two games to take notice, but the Nebraska men’s basketball team earned a well-deserved spot at No. 25 in this week’s AP Top 25.
--> It may have taken AP voters two games to take notice, but the Nebraska men’s basketball team earned a well-deserved spot at No. 25 in this week’s AP Top 25.
 That's because the Cornhuskers are coming off a solid early-season victory against NCAA Tournament dark horse Providence, 67-58 Saturday afternoon in the Hall of Fame Tip-Off. Nebraska's defense came through in a big way by scoring 20 points off 18 Friar turnovers and holding their fast-paced offense to a 30.6% mark from the field.

 Star forward Pryce Sandfort carried the Huskers' offense with a game-high 25 points, including a trio of three-pointers. Boden Kapke scored 13 points while grabbing five rebounds. Guard Braden Frager struggled from the field, but the Lincoln native still added 12 points with four steals, while Cale Jacobsen chipped in 11.

 After leading Lindenwood through the transition from Division II to Division I, head coach Kyle Gerdeman has found solid footing with the Lions after two poor seasons at the top level of college sports. Following back-to-back seasons that saw Lindenwood go a combined 20-43, the Lions have bounced back with seasons of 15-16 and 18-15 for a 33-31 record. 
--> After leading Lindenwood through the transition from Division II to Division I, head coach Kyle Gerdeman has found solid footing with the Lions after two poor seasons at the top level of college sports. Following back-to-back seasons that saw Lindenwood go a combined 20-43, the Lions have bounced back with seasons of 15-16 and 18-15 for a 33-31 record. 
 Unfortunately for Gerdeman, every single member of his most successful roster at Lindenwood is now gone. That includes All-OVC First Team picks Anias Futrell (Graduation) and Jadis Jones (USC). Starting guards Dontrez Williams and Mekhi Cooper followed Jones by transferring to bigger programs in UNLV and Louisiana, while 6-foot-11 center Milos Nenadic graduated after scoring 12 points per game and grabbing six rebounds.

 That forced Gerdeman to pull off a complete rebuilding of the roster going into the 2026-2027 season. Leading that pack has been Fresno State forward Mekhan Diouf with over 15 PPG despite playing in only two of the team's three contests this season. The same goes for reserve Kellen Robinson, who's averaging 12.5 points per game through two contests despite playing at Little Rock during his freshman campaign.

One of the rare midseason transfers last season, Malek Archie joined the Lions from Tarleton State and now averages 12 points per contest through three games this year. Senior guard Xavier Spencer leads the team with 72 minutes played after pouring in nearly 12 PPG as a starter at UMass Lowell last season. Joining the Lions after two seasons coming off the bench for LMU, guard Noah Taitz has seen over 21 minutes per game this year as a non-starter.
 A pair of players with a Nebraska connection both return to a state with basketball beginnings. Forward Matar Diop was a freshman on Fred Hoiberg's first NCAA Tournament team in 2024 that lost to Texas A&M in the first round. He spent one season at LMU and one year at Stetson before joining Lindenwood for his fourth school in as many years. Plus, freshman forward Derek Rollins returns after playing his high school career at Millard North. He's one of the team's leading rebounders so far through three games with over five per contest. 6-foot-11 freshman center Parker Seithel helps in that department with over five per game as well, including an 11-rebound performance last time out against East-West University — which is a real school.

 I'm impressed by Gerdeman's work in the transfer portal, but Lindenwood will be a team that should experience more mid-season development than most other squads knowing the turnover they had. Wednesday will be a learning lesson for the Lions, who will try to surprise people this season after being tabbed to finish sixth in the OVC preseason poll. Put me down for a massive Nebraska win.
